questions.question: AES canonical has been on hold since 2026-10-18 after the ~/code2 move to off-the-shelf tools. Should it stay on hold (kept as a working library two repositories still call), resume as a product, or be retired and archived?
questions.blocks: whether any plan beyond keeping the repository's own checks honest is worth doing here, and whether dodaf and whygame5 should keep calling aes
questions.resolves_with: Brian's priority call; no check settles it. The facts that bear on it are recorded: the value tally came back at 1 catch and 6 hand checks (Decision 0011), and 2 of 12 criteria are supported today (make aes).
questions.recommendation: Keep it on hold. Run only the hygiene plan (docs/planning/next.goal.md) so the repository tells the truth about itself, and leave the aes CLI working for dodaf and whygame5.
questions.default: AES stays on hold; agents run the hygiene plan and nothing else here.

questions.question: The durable-documents check fails with CATALOG-STALE because generated/docstring_wiki.md was not regenerated after later commits. Is regenerating it all that is needed?

The fix is `make docstring-wiki` and a commit, then rerun the check; it is open only because this package touches docs/planning/ alone. Open as a work item only: the answer is known, and a check that still fails must point at an open question.

questions.short: Evidence went stale after the commit rule's removal
questions.question: Decision 0010 accepted v0.2 with its nine criteria supported; `make aes` at c1b3ee6 reports 2 of 12 supported and 50 of 82 observations stale. Three criteria were added after the acceptance (SC-TR-001, SC-ADOPT-001, SC-TR-SOURCE-001), and 15 observations depend on commit_rule.py, which a06e963 deleted (docs and target updated in bb6818a). Is the staleness only that, or did a change break one of the nine accepted criteria?
questions.blocks: whether `aes status` can be quoted as the product's state, and whether Decision 0010's acceptance still stands
questions.resolves_with: Running the existing verification subjects settles it, no new evaluation: `aes evidence record <VS-ID>` for each deterministic-test subject behind the nine Decision 0010 criteria re-runs its named tests at HEAD; all passing means the evidence was only stale, and any failure is a regression with a named test. The three later criteria are listed separately with the evidence kind each needs: SC-TR-SOURCE-001 needs a trace_review (ER-TR-SOURCE-002) and SC-GF-001 a runtime_observation (a clean-user run), which re-recording tests cannot give. The unreachable accepted plan PLAN-AES-SELF-GOVERN stays a warning by design (reconcile.py lines 18-20).

questions.question: The repository holds 213 tracked Markdown files at c1b3ee6 (210 on main plus this package's three; its cold review adds a fourth) against its own 140-file exception (written 2026-10-07 at about 130, 146 a day later). Move the superseded plan bundles to ~/archive (after a content check, restore steps recorded) only where nothing cites them; raise the limit, with the count of cited files as its reason, for the rest. questions.short: Not in the code2 repository format
questions.question: ~/code2/AGENTS.md brings each repository into the code2 format when it is next changed; scripts/repo_format.py reports this one 0 of 1 compliant (missing docs/index.md, arc42, a .c4 model, OpenSpec specs, a code2check Makefile target). Does the hygiene plan adopt the format, or defer it?
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it: the rule applies when the repository is next changed, and the hygiene plan changes it, so the plan adds the items that cost minutes (docs/index.md pointing at wiki/index.md, a code2check target running make aes and the link check) and records the rest (arc42, .c4, OpenSpec specs) as deferred while AES is on hold, each with that reason.

questions.question: Does AES evaluate typed rules (relations with named roles whose effects run), which would need a type-level metamodel mapped onto the shared kernel?
